title: ACOG — Women's Health
publisher: American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists
why: The body that sets US prenatal care standards. Start here for anything about appointments, screening windows, or symptoms.

title: CDC — Pregnancy
publisher: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
why: Vaccines, infections, and the things that are genuinely risky in pregnancy, in plain language.

title: CDC — Immunization schedules
publisher: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
why: The schedule your pediatrician is following. Useful when you want to know what is coming and why.

title: Milestones by age
publisher: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
why: What most children do by each age, and the specific things worth asking about. Written to inform, not to score.

title: HealthyChildren.org
why: The AAP's parent-facing site. The most reliable plain-language answer to a pediatric question.

title: March of Dimes
why: Pregnancy and newborn health, with a strong section on preterm birth and what to expect if it happens.

title: NICHD
why: The research arm. Go here when you want the study behind a claim rather than a summary of it.

title: MotherToBaby
why: Free, evidence-based answers on whether a medication or exposure is safe in pregnancy and while breastfeeding.

title: LactMed
why: The drug-by-drug database for breastfeeding. What to check before you take anything.

title: Safe to Sleep
why: The safe-sleep rules, from the agency that funds the research behind them.

title: NHTSA — Car seats and booster seats
why: Ease-of-use ratings, the current recommendations, and where to get a free installation check. A seat that installs correctly every time beats a seat with better test numbers.

title: CPSC — Recalls
why: The official recall list. Check anything secondhand before it goes in the nursery.

title: 16 CFR 1219 — Full-size cribs
why: The actual federal crib standard. Dense, but it is the thing a crib has to meet to be legal to sell.

title: Tips for Infant Formula Feeding
publisher: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
why: How to mix, store and warm formula safely, and when to throw it out.

title: Office on Women's Health — Breastfeeding
publisher: US Department of Health and Human Services
why: A calm, complete starting point, including your right to pump at work.

title: CDC — Infant and toddler nutrition
publisher: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
why: When to start solids, what to offer, and the foods to avoid in the first year.

title: WIC
why: Food benefits for pregnancy and the first years. Income limits are higher than most people assume.

title: SNAP
why: The larger food program. Applying takes about twenty minutes and does not affect immigration status for most families.

title: Medicaid — Pregnancy coverage
why: Pregnancy Medicaid covers far more people than standard Medicaid. Worth checking even if you think you earn too much.

title: InsureKidsNow — CHIP
why: Low-cost or free coverage for a child, separate from the parents' plan.

title: DOL — FMLA
why: Twelve weeks of job-protected leave, and who actually qualifies. The eligibility rules surprise people.

title: IRS — Child Tax Credit
why: What you can claim and when. A new baby changes your withholding, not just your refund.

title: 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline
publisher: Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration
why: Call or text 988, any hour. For intrusive thoughts, panic, or the feeling that you cannot do this.

title: National Maternal Mental Health Hotline
why: 1-833-TLC-MAMA. Staffed by people trained for pregnancy and postpartum specifically, 24 hours.

title: Poison Control
why: 1-800-222-1222. Free, 24 hours, and faster than the internet for a swallowed button battery or a mouthful of diaper cream.

title: Postpartum Support International
why: A helpline, free support groups, and a provider directory. The first place to go when it is more than the baby blues.

title: NAMI
why: Support groups and family programs, including ones for partners who are struggling.

title: ZERO TO THREE
why: Development from a baby's point of view. The best writing on what is actually happening in the first three years.

title: ASHA — Speech and language
why: What is typical at each age, and how to tell a delay from a difference.

title: CDC — Autism
publisher: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
why: The signs, the screening schedule, and what early intervention actually looks like.

title: ECTA Center — Early Intervention
why: How to request a free developmental evaluation under IDEA Part C. You can self-refer in every state.

title: NAEYC
publisher: National Association for the Education of Young Children
why: What a good early-childhood program looks like, and how accreditation works.

title: Child Care Aware
why: A searchable directory of licensed care by ZIP code, plus the questions worth asking on a tour.

title: Head Start
why: Free early education for eligible families, including Early Head Start for under-threes.

title: Nurse-Family Partnership
why: A free nurse who visits through pregnancy and the first two years. First-time, low-income parents are eligible.

title: Safe Kids Worldwide
why: Free car seat checks and home safety events, searchable by ZIP code.

title: Cribs for Kids
why: A safe sleep space for families who cannot afford one. Ask your hospital social worker.

title: La Leche League
why: Free peer support, in person and by phone. Useful at 2am when the latch still hurts.

title: USLCA — Find a lactation consultant
why: An IBCLC is the credential that matters. Many insurance plans cover the visit at no cost.

title: DONA International
why: A doula is continuous support, not a medical role. This is the largest certifying body.

title: American College of Nurse-Midwives
why: How to find a certified nurse-midwife, and what their scope of practice actually is.

title: ICAN
why: For a VBAC question, or for processing a birth that did not go the way you planned.

title: Fed is Best Foundation
why: For when breastfeeding is not working and the advice you are getting is making it worse.

title: Solid Starts
why: A free food database showing how to serve each food safely at each age. The choking guidance is specific and correct.
One number for local help: food, rent, utilities, childcare, counseling. Dial 211 or search by ZIP.

title: SaferProducts.gov
why: Report a product that hurt your child, and read what other parents reported.

title: CDC — Lead prevention
publisher: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
why: Older housing, imported toys, and the blood test that is easy to skip.

title: CDC — Drowning prevention
publisher: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
why: Drowning is the leading cause of death for children 1 to 4. The layers of protection, in order.

title: Milestones by 2 months
why: What most babies do by two months, and the one thing to ask about if something looks different.

title: Milestones by 4 months
why: The four-month list, including the social smile and head control a visit will check.

title: Milestones by 6 months
why: Sitting with support, babbling, and reaching. The list a six-month visit works from.

title: Milestones by 9 months
why: Nine months is when pincer grasp and stranger awareness show up. Here is the full list.

title: Milestones by 1 year
why: Pulling to stand, first words, and drinking from a cup. What a one-year visit looks for.

title: Milestones by 15 months
why: Walking, a few words, and pointing to ask. The list behind the 15-month check.

title: Milestones by 18 months
why: The 18-month list, including the autism screen most pediatricians run at this visit.

title: Milestones by 2 years
why: Two-word phrases, running, and copying. What the two-year visit is measuring.

title: Milestones by 30 months
why: The 30-month list. Short, specific, and the one most parents have never seen.

title: Milestones by 3 years
why: Sentences, stairs, and pretend play. What a three-year visit checks before preschool.

title: Learn the Signs. Act Early.
why: The whole developmental screening programme, with free checklists you can print and take to a visit.

title: Breastfeeding recommendations
why: What the US recommends on duration and exclusivity, and where the evidence is thin.

title: Healthy habits for child development
why: The everyday things that move development along, written for a parent rather than a clinician.

title: Staying healthy during pregnancy
why: ACOG's own index for the middle of pregnancy: nutrition, exercise, sleep, travel, warning signs.

title: After pregnancy
why: Recovery, the postpartum visit, birth control, and how long the bleeding and soreness last.

title: Labor and delivery
why: Induction, pain relief, cesarean, and what the last weeks of pregnancy actually look like.

title: Getting pregnant
why: For the early weeks, when the first question is often what happens at the first visit.

title: Exercise during pregnancy
why: How much, how hard, and the short list of things to stop doing. Answers the gym question.

title: Travel during pregnancy
why: When flying is fine, when it is not, and what to do about a long car trip.

title: Back pain during pregnancy
why: Why it happens, what helps, and the red flags that mean it is something else.

title: Breastfeeding your baby
why: Getting started, how to tell the baby is getting enough, and when to call for help.

title: Postpartum birth control
why: What is safe while breastfeeding, and how soon fertility can return. A question nobody asks out loud.

title: Cesarean birth
why: What a cesarean involves, what recovery is like, and what a repeat pregnancy might mean.

title: Early pregnancy loss
why: What happens, what the options are, and that it is not caused by anything you did.

title: Preterm labor and birth
why: The signs to act on, and what happens if a baby arrives early.

title: Pain relief in labor
why: Epidural, nitrous, and unmedicated options, explained without a side in the argument.

title: Depression and anxiety in pregnancy and after
why: An OB writing plainly about what she tells patients, and why treatment is not a last resort.

title: A high-risk pregnancy
why: What the label means, what changes about your care, and what does not.

title: The RSV vaccine in pregnancy
why: Why it is offered in a narrow window late in pregnancy, and what it protects.

title: Prenatal health
why: The pediatrician's view of pregnancy, which is a different angle from your OB's.

title: Baby nutrition
why: AAP's feeding index: formula, solids, allergies, and how much is enough.

title: Baby sleep
why: Safe sleep, sleep patterns by age, and what to do about a baby who will not settle.

title: Safety at home
why: Room by room, what to fix before a baby becomes mobile.

title: Safety at play
why: Outdoors, water, wheels, and playgrounds, with the age each risk starts.

title: Screen time and media
why: AAP's screen guidance by age, including what to do instead and why it is not a moral failing.

title: Pregnancy
why: Plain-language summaries with links to the primary sources, for when you want to read further.

title: Toddler health
why: A broad index of toddler health topics, written at a reading level a tired parent can manage.

title: Child behaviour
why: What is a phase and what is worth asking about, with the clinical names for both.

title: Pregnancy
why: Federal guidance on pregnancy written for patients, including the parts about money and work.

title: Mental health
why: Depression, anxiety, and where to get help, including free and low-cost options.

title: Perinatal depression
why: The clinical picture, the difference from the baby blues, and the treatments that work.

title: Pregnancy research
why: For a parent who wants the research rather than the advice. Dense, but honest about uncertainty.

title: Breastfeeding and breast milk
why: What the evidence says about milk, supply, and the things that do and do not affect either.

title: Pumping at work
why: The federal right to break time and a private space, and who it does not cover.

title: Earned Income Tax Credit
why: A credit many eligible families never claim. Worth ten minutes with last year's return.

title: Office of Child Care
why: Federal childcare help, including the subsidy programme most states run under a different name.

title: Social Security disability
why: For a family where a parent cannot work. Slow, paperwork-heavy, and worth starting early.

title: Food assistance
why: One page that routes to SNAP, WIC, school meals, and food banks by state.

title: Find government benefits
why: A short questionnaire that lists what your household may qualify for. Ten minutes, no account.

title: USAGov
why: The front door to federal services, for the questions that do not fit anywhere else.

title: Department of Health and Human Services
why: The parent agency for most of the health programmes here, with state-level links.

title: US Department of Agriculture
why: Food programmes, nutrition guidance, and the WIC and SNAP pages in one place.

title: Health Insurance Marketplace
why: Coverage, pregnancy as a qualifying event, and what a plan has to cover for a birth.

title: Pathways.org
why: Free milestone checklists and activity ideas by age, with a strong focus on the first year.

title: AAP — American Academy of Pediatrics
why: The academy that writes the schedule your pediatrician follows. Policy statements, in full.
